symptom: The first `lint` (or `verify`) after `mxcli exec` changed the model reported "MPR017 could not run: read 35 entities but could not read their attributes" and a bogus new warning; the three real MPR017 findings were counted as fixed in the baseline comparison. An identical second run, with no change in between, was right. Reproduced every time on a copy of ako/ChipCoV14 (exec adds an attribute, then lint); ako/mxcli#2454, a recurrence of #2417.
cause: An incremental catalog build loads the cached catalog into ONE pooled connection with sqlite3_deserialize (builder.go buildOn), which gives that connection a PRIVATE copy of its main database and detaches it from the in-memory shared cache. Every other pooled connection still sees the original shared-cache database: its tables exist and hold no rows. Reads made one statement at a time are served by the connection that holds the data, so every table-equality test passed; a read made while another cursor is open (lint's ctx.Entities() loop calling ctx.AttributesFor(), i.e. MPR017 and MPR018) needs a second connection and got zero rows with NO error. Measured with a temporary debug build of lint: the catalog held all 254 attributes, AttributesFor returned 24 called one entity at a time and 0 called inside the Entities() cursor. #2417 had fixed this for the full build only, which writes through the shared cache.
file: `mdl/catalog/builder.go` (buildOn), `mdl/catalog/catalogdb_sqlite.go` (adoptPrivateCopy, retireConn, the new dsn field); test `mdl/executor/catalog_incremental_nested_reads_pedapp_test.go`.
insight: A catalog test that reads one statement at a time cannot see a database split across connections: TestCatalog_IncrementalBuildEqualsFullBuild compared every table of an incremental build with a full one and was green while a nested read returned nothing. The signature is 'no error, zero rows, only on the first run after a write, and the same query is right once the catalog is loaded from the cache file'; stop reading the rule and ask whether the second connection sees the same database. The discriminating measurement was one line in a scratch build of lint: count the same rows sequentially and nested. The fix copies the private database back into the shared cache with SQLite's online backup (page-level, so carried rows are still not re-inserted) and marks the build connection bad so the pool drops it; leaving it pooled would keep answering from a private copy that later writes do not reach. Any rule that nests reads is exposed to this class, and a rule that cannot read its input reported it as a finding of its own rule, which the lint baseline then counted as new while counting the rule's real findings as fixed (ako/mxcli#2455 is the same gap: the baseline has no notion of which rules ran).
